body.content:
## Introduction

If you are planning to make your team remote, the first practical step is defining how you will work together. A clear operating model is key to a smooth transition.

![Illustration of a distributed team working online](/api/assets/blogs/remote-work-guide/01.webp)

## What Does Your Remote Model Look Like?

For most organisations there is no single template. Choose the model that fits your goals and culture:

| Model | Meetings | Best For |
|-------|----------|----------|
| **Fully remote** | Asynchronous by default | Globally distributed teams |
| **Hybrid** | Weekly in-office days | Teams that value in-person time |

## Basic Setup

1. **Written communication norms** — Define which channels are for async updates vs. real-time
2. **A shared task tracker** — Single source of truth for what's in flight
3. **Clear availability hours** — Overlap windows across time zones
4. **Documented onboarding** — A repeatable first-week for every hire
5. **Tooling budget** — Laptops, licenses and an allowance for home office setups
6. **Feedback cadence** — Regular 1:1s and retrospectives

## Step-by-Step Transition

### Step 1: Define Principles and Goals

Before choosing tools, agree on how you want to work and what success looks like.

### Step 2: Choose Your Toolkit

Select a small set of tools for chat, video, documents and project tracking, and document how they are used.

### Step 3: Set Communication Norms

Decide what is async, what is synchronous, and how urgent issues escalate.

### Step 4: Communicate the Plan

Announce the policy, timelines and expectations clearly to the whole team.

### Step 5: Roll Out, Measure and Iterate

Launch gradually, collect feedback and adjust the model over the first few months.

## Costs (2026)

| Item | Cost (USD) | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|
| Common tooling | $15-$40 / user / month | Varies by provider and seats |
| Home-office allowance | $500-$1,500 one-off | Per newly remote employee |
| Team meetups | Varies | 1-2 in-person offsites a year |

> **Note:** Switching to remote typically saves on office space while adding a small per-employee tooling cost.

## Tips for a Smooth Rollout

1. **Start with async-first** — Reduce meeting load from day one
2. **Over-communicate early** — More context beats less during the transition
3. **Invest in onboarding** — The first 30 days set expectations for everything after
4. **Make time zones visible** — Keep a shared calendar and respect boundaries

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How long does a remote rollout take?
A typical rollout takes 4-8 weeks. Stand up the toolkit and norms first, then transition teams in cohorts.

### Can we mix remote with in-office?
Yes — a hybrid model works well when you set clear in-office days and keep asynchronous defaults.

### Is remote collaboration tooling expensive?
Not necessarily. A small, well-adopted toolset costs $15-$40 per user per month and replaces most ad-hoc spend.

## Conclusion

Making the jump to remote is straightforward when you have the right operating model. The key is proper preparation — defining norms early and building documentation so new hires succeed.

With YourBrand's support, you can navigate the transition confidently and focus on what matters.
